descriptions.client: Generates the offered load (requests/s) that drives the whole system. Connect its output to your first tier (API gateway, load balancer or server). Tune "Base rate" to set how many requests per second enter the system.
descriptions.loadBalancer: Spreads incoming requests across the downstream replicas it points to, using the selected strategy (round-robin, least-connections, weighted or consistent hashing). Place it between the client/gateway and a pool of servers.
descriptions.apiGateway: Single entry point at the edge of your system. Enforces a requests/s rate limit — traffic above the limit is dropped — and forwards the rest to backends. Connect the client to it, and it to your services.
descriptions.cache: Serves a fraction of reads from memory set by "Hit rate". Hits return quickly; misses fall through to the downstream store. Put it in front of a database or service to cut load and latency.
descriptions.server: Stateless compute tier that processes requests with a given service time and concurrency. Scale it with replicas or front it with an auto-scaler. Connect it to databases, caches or other services it depends on.
descriptions.database: Persistent datastore and an end point (no outgoing edges). Its service time and concurrency make it a common bottleneck. Send read/write traffic from servers into it.
descriptions.replicatedDb: Database with multiple replicas. Writes (set by "Write fraction") hit the primary; reads spread across replicas. Pick a consistency level (strong/quorum/eventual) and replication lag to model trade-offs.
descriptions.shardRouter: Partitions traffic across shards by key using hash or range strategy. "Hot-shard skew" models one shard receiving disproportionate load. Connect it to a pool of shard backends.
descriptions.messageQueue: Buffers incoming requests and drains them at a fixed rate to smooth spikes. Messages beyond the queue capacity are dropped. Place it between a fast producer and a slower consumer.
descriptions.circuitBreaker: Wraps a downstream dependency. When the error rate exceeds the threshold it opens and sheds load for the reset timeout, then half-opens to probe recovery. Use it to stop cascading failures.
descriptions.autoScaler: Adjusts the replica count of the tier it fronts to keep utilization near the target, bounded by min/max replicas. Use it to react automatically to changing load.
descriptions.externalDependency: A third-party service you do not control (an end point). Model its latency and failure rate to simulate outages or slowdowns of upstream providers.

hints.label: Display name for this node on the canvas. Does not affect the simulation.
hints.base_rate: Requests per second this client generates. Higher = more load on the whole system; lower = lighter traffic.
hints.cron: Turn this service into a scheduled (cron) source: it generates its own work on a timer and needs no incoming connection. Use it for cron jobs, recurring workers and periodic producers.
hints.cron_rate: Self-generated requests per second when cron is on. Higher = more scheduled work injected; lower = a lighter periodic trickle.
hints.auto_scalable: Let this service scale its own replicas at runtime to hold the target utilization, bounded by min/max replicas — no separate auto-scaler node needed.
hints.service_time: Milliseconds to process one request (sets the service rate µ). Higher = slower per request, lower capacity and higher latency; lower = faster and more throughput.
hints.concurrency: Parallel workers per replica (the c in M/M/c). Higher = more requests served at once, less queueing and lower latency; lower = saturates sooner.
hints.replicas: Number of identical copies of this node (horizontal scaling). Higher = proportionally more capacity; lower = less capacity.
hints.failure_rate: Baseline probability a request fails here regardless of load. Higher = more errors propagated downstream; lower = more reliable.
hints.timeout: Milliseconds before a slow request is counted as failed. Lower = more timeouts when the node is busy; higher = waits longer before giving up.
hints.max_retries: How many times a failed call is retried. Higher = fewer final errors but more amplified load (retry storms); lower = less load but more user-visible failures.
hints.distribution: Shape of the per-request latency distribution. Lognormal has a realistic heavy tail, exponential is memoryless, deterministic is constant.
hints.variability: Coefficient of variation of latency (lognormal only). Higher = heavier tail, so p95/p99 grow; lower = more uniform latencies.
hints.strategy: How incoming requests are spread across downstream replicas (round-robin, least-connections, weighted, or consistent hashing).
hints.rate_limit: Maximum requests per second admitted; anything above is dropped. Higher = fewer drops but more load downstream; lower = protects backends but rejects traffic.
hints.hit_rate: Fraction of reads served from cache. Higher = much less load and latency downstream; lower = more requests fall through to the store.
hints.ttl: How long cached entries stay valid. Higher = more hits but staler data; lower = fresher data but more misses.
hints.queue_capacity: Maximum messages buffered. Higher = absorbs bigger spikes without dropping, but adds backlog latency; lower = drops sooner under overload.
hints.drain_rate: Messages consumed per second. Higher = backlog clears faster and latency drops; lower = backlog builds up.
hints.write_fraction: Share of operations that are writes. Higher = more load on the single primary (writes serialize), lowering effective capacity; lower = reads dominate and scale across replicas.
hints.replication_lag: Milliseconds replicas trail the primary. Higher = more stale reads with eventual consistency; lower = fresher replicas.
hints.consistency: Read/write guarantee. Strong is safest but slowest, quorum balances, eventual is fastest but can read stale data.
hints.shard_count: Number of partitions traffic is split across. Higher = more parallel capacity; lower = each shard carries more load.
hints.skew: How unevenly load lands on the hottest shard. Higher = one shard saturates and caps effective capacity; lower = balanced load.
hints.shard_strategy: How keys map to shards. Hash spreads evenly; range keeps neighbouring keys together (more prone to hotspots).
hints.error_threshold: Downstream error rate that trips the breaker open. Lower = opens sooner to protect the dependency; higher = tolerates more errors first.
hints.reset_timeout: Milliseconds the breaker stays open before probing recovery. Higher = waits longer before retrying; lower = retries the dependency sooner.
hints.target_utilization: Utilization the auto-scaler tries to hold. Lower = scales out earlier (more replicas, more headroom); higher = runs hotter with fewer replicas.
hints.min_replicas: Lower bound on replicas the auto-scaler will keep, even when idle.
hints.max_replicas: Upper bound on replicas the auto-scaler can add under load.

rules.service_present: keep at least one app server
rules.path_to_db: every client must reach a database through your service tier
rules.cache_miss_path: every cache needs a miss path to a database
rules.no_client_to_db: clients cannot talk to the database directly
